## Retired generated skills are no longer injectable; the backlog is reconciled

Explicit `SKILLS: file:` references to retired or stale generated skills are now
blocked at delegation time with a named replacement. Previously the
explicit-reference validator checked only path shape, containment, existence,
frontmatter, and audience — so a retired skill (whose `retired.marker` directory
marker discovery and routing already respected) validated and the delegation
proceeded carrying stale instructions, including a retired worktree-cleanup variant
that instructed removing the session worktree PARENT and a gate-attribution variant
that inverted the native per-task counting rule. Marker text is sanitized and
length-bounded before entering the architect-visible refusal.

Five historical slugs receive a consumer-stable replacement pointing at the bundled
canon materialized under `.swarm/bundled-skills/` (`gate-attribution`,
`merge-queue-readiness`, `skill-edit-validation`, `worktree-retry-cleanup`, and
`pr-review-fix` → `swarm-pr-feedback`); every other retired/stale slug gets an
actionable regenerate/inspect instruction. Both the symlink target's directory and
the lexical directory are checked (a marker on either side of a symlink blocks).

This repository's generated-skill backlog was reconciled: 19 retired forks and the
active bundled-slug collision `ci-failure-batching` were removed from
`.opencode/skills/generated/` (17 legitimate active forks remain), and the Codex
adapters that still designated retired forks as canonical were repointed —
`mock-to-internals-migration` is now a self-contained `.agents` canon and
`test-file-split` describes the extraction pattern inline in all three trees.
Consumer projects get the gate automatically.

---

## Lean Turbo lane planning now applies the Rule-3 upstream-commit gate under Epic Mode

Under Epic Mode, Lean Turbo lane planning now refuses to place a task in a parallel
lane when its cross-phase `depends:` upstream has no `swarm(task <id>):` landing
commit in the open Epic's commit range for the current plan — the task is degraded
with a named remediation (`cross-batch upstream not committed (greenfield-smart
Rule 3): <id>`) instead of being dispatched against missing work. The predicate was
always reserved as the planner's final parameter but no production caller supplied
it, so every cross-batch dependency was silently treated as satisfied.

The evidence reuses the current Epic marker machinery (`findTaskCommits`):
merge-inclusive (coder landings are `--no-ff` merges), filtered by the
`Swarm-Plan:` trailer (task ids repeat across plans), and scrub-id aware. The wiring
is epic-gated through `isEpicOpenForProject` — pure Lean Turbo behavior is
unchanged (predicate `undefined`, byte-identical placement), and the affected path
is direct/composition Lean invocation while an Epic is open (sanctioned flows keep
Epic and Turbo mutually exclusive). An unborn HEAD (empty repository) yields a
defined predicate with an empty committed set; a genuine git failure degrades to
the disclosed legacy behavior with an operator-visible warning.

Also corrected: the stale `planLeanTurboLanes` JSDoc claim that production callers
build the predicate from a builder that was deleted from the tree, and the Epic
maintainer guide now documents the new Lean→Epic consumer seam.

# Receipt-footer aggregate-bounds test no longer times out under coverage

## What changed

The per-test timeout on `bounds aggregate large valid receipts while retaining
every anti-replay tombstone` in
`tests/unit/tools/dispatch-lanes-pr-review-receipt-footer.test.ts` was raised
from 30 000 ms to 60 000 ms, matching the coverage gate's own per-test budget
(`bun test --isolate --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov --timeout 60000` in
`scripts/ci/run-coverage-gate.sh`). A new lockstep pin
(`tests/unit/scripts/ci/ci-coverage-timeout-lockstep.test.ts`) fails CI if the
test's explicit cap ever diverges from the gate's budget. No production code
changed.

## Why

A per-test timeout overrides `bun test --timeout`, so the coverage gate never
got to apply its own 60 s per-test budget to this test: the old 30 s cap
killed it first. The corpus is intentionally large (80 delegations × 180
review-item IDs through real SQLite-backed transitions plus two forced
compactions). Between 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-27 the flake detector recorded
**nine** detections of this file (seven via #3264, two via #3263), including
hard shard failures on 2026-10-25 (run 40152945255, coverage-shard (5)),
three same-day failures on 2026-10-26 (runs 40253942931, 40255972796 and
40282456510 — coverage-shard (6) for all three, five green merge-group CI
runs separating the last two), and a 3/3-attempt hard failure on
2026-10-27 (run 40449933636, coverage-shard (5)). Coverage shards are
Linux-only and shard indices are a per-run partition.
Every observed figure (30.2–32.0 s) is a **censored elapsed time at the kill**
— no instrumented run of this test has completed on CI — so the 60 s cap is
sized at ~1.9× above the highest censored observation, equals the gate's own
budget, and the first post-fix green run yields the first true completed
measurement (the merge-group coverage shards run on the self-hosted Linux
fleet).

## Migration steps

None. The change is a test-file timeout raise plus a lockstep pin.

## Known caveats

- This file is a repeat offender (nine detections), and quarantine was still
  deliberately rejected: the coverage gate reads only the general ledger, so
  an entry would also drop the file from the ubuntu unit shards and lose real
  coverage of `src/background/pr-review-collection-receipt.ts`. If the test
  ever exceeds 60 s instrumented, the remedy is shrinking the corpus (while
  keeping the shedding property asserted), not raising the cap again.
- The other #3263 candidates: five of the six issue-body files are the
  pre-fix `.swarm/` checkout-posture wave root-fixed by the #3248 cohort
  (named with their detection counts in `scripts/ci/run-coverage-gate.sh`);
  `tests/unit/hooks/delegation-gate-retry-sounding-board-manual.test.ts` is a
  CORE-TREE candidate that still awaits its per-file human decision on #3263
  (rule C of `scripts/ci/detect-and-quarantine-flakes.sh`).
  `tests/unit/commands/archive-dry-run.test.ts` was detected twice (2026-10-18
  via #3264 run 39108262782; 2026-10-26 via #3263 run 40282456510) as a
  passed-on-retry Windows teardown flake whose raw-`rmSync` root cause is
  tracked under open #3252; it gets no ledger entry unless recurrence beyond
  #3252's fix warrants one.
<!-- custom-release-notes:end -->

# Guardrails: shell-audit rows record real targets, and the rmdir /s check follows cmd.exe's actual grammar

## What

Closes #3495 and #3345 (collated; both are the guardrails shell-write surface).
Includes the feedback-round fixes from the PR #3499 review.

When the shell write-scope gate denies a command, the `scope_violation` row in
`.swarm/session/shell-audit.jsonl` now records the actual blocked write target
in `path` and the write operator that tripped the gate in a new optional
`operator` field, for the five structured denial sites (declared-scope,
file-authority, universal-deny, inline-eval, dynamic-path). Denials that carry
no target (no active agent, scope not declared) keep the previous
message-derived row. The denial message for the scope gate also names its gate
(`WRITE BLOCKED [shell-write-scope]: …`) so an operator can tell it apart from
the destructive-command gate in a transcript. Persisted `path` fields are
bounded at 320 chars and the new `operator` field at 32 (embedded paths
redacted), so no persisted audit field is unbounded — previously an
oversized value could make the bounded store reject the whole line.

The Windows recursive-delete check now models cmd.exe's actual grammar
(verified against real cmd.exe): cmd scans each UNQUOTED argument for the
first `/` — everything after it is switch text, the text before it is the
path. So the recursion switch is recognized standalone (`rmdir /s x`),
clustered (`/s/q`, `/sq`), trailing (`rd x /s`), attached to the operand
(`rd zzz/s` = `rd zzz /s`), caret-escaped (`rmdir ^/^s zzz`), single-quoted
(`rmdir 'zzz/s'` — cmd does not honor single quotes), or glued to a quoted
operand (`del /s"file.txt"`); a switch with no operand fails closed. A `/s`
substring inside an operand whose post-slash text is NOT a valid switch name
(`rmdir a/share/b` — cmd itself rejects it with "Parameter format not
correct") is a plain nested path, so the #3456 nested-path cleanup works
again. The `/swarm guardrail-explain` mirror uses the same grammar, and the
write detector defers an `rmdir` to the destructive guard only when the
guard will actually evaluate it — a quoted `"/s"` is a path, so the
remaining operands reach the scope gate instead of being skipped by both
layers.

`tests/unit/hooks/guardrails-shell-write.test.ts` declares explicit 120 s
per-test timeouts on its redirect/move/sed-i family tests, so bare local runs
on loaded hosts no longer flake against bun's 5 s default. The in-code cap
equals CI's per-file `--timeout 120000` budget (an in-code per-test cap
overrides the CLI value, so CI is never shrunk by it).

## Why

The audit row is the operator-facing evidence of what the gate refused;
recording `SCOPE_VIOLATION:` as the path made `guardrail-log --blocks-only`
unanswerable without reading transcripts. The `/s` over-match blocked
legitimate nested-path cleanup — and the first cut of the token fix still
missed cmd.exe's attached-switch grammar (`rd zzz/s` is a real recursive
delete), which this round closes.

---

# Preserve interrupted coder settlement work

Coder settlement recovery now retains surviving recorded source commits even
when a lane checkout and branch are missing. Merge recovery can resume on a
compatible advanced primary branch while retaining conflict, dirty-overlap and
source-identity checks. Pending settlements protect their artifacts from
cleanup through shared dispatch/deletion admission. That protection covers
dispatch and lane cleanup performed by the plugin; it does not cover an
explicit `/swarm close`, which archives the session and then removes the
`.swarm/coder-settlements/` directory.

Mixed foreground/background completion now hands off settlement ownership
before removing the lane. Interrupted handoff and leftover cleanup can replay
from saved provenance without merging twice; changed lanes remain preserved
for manual recovery.

Recovery also detects the specific historical missing-worktree self-heal that
may already have marked a settlement aborted. It reports the exact recoverable
commit and retained backup ref without reviving an old task generation. That
`RECOVERABLE_ORPHAN_COMMIT` report is advisory: task status, re-dispatch and
close are not blocked by it. Committed recovery releases its backup; unstaged
work and historical work that has not landed by ancestry remain retained for
explicit operator review. See
[coder settlement recovery](../../coder-settlement-recovery.md) for discovery
and safe cleanup commands.

No settlement schema or configuration migration is required.

# Fix: macOS sandbox profile embeds kernel-resolved system paths

## What changed

The macOS `sandbox-exec` profile builder now writes the kernel-resolved form of a path when it starts with one of the three macOS system links: `/tmp`, `/var` and `/etc` become `/private/tmp`, `/private/var` and `/private/etc`. The rewrite applies to scope paths and to the temp dir, in both the production and the probe profile, and only when this host's `realpath` confirms the link.

The rewrite is a prefix swap on the input string. No other symlink is ever followed, so a link created inside a project can neither change the result nor widen the profile to its target. A path that is already resolved is used as it is. A path under any other symlink (for example `~/projects -> /Volumes/data`), a host without the link, or an error leaves the path exactly as written (the previous behaviour): that path stays unmatched by Seatbelt and writes to it are denied.

Seatbelt matches `subpath` against the kernel-resolved path. Before this change a scoped `(allow file-write* (subpath "/var/…"))` line never matched, so the allow was inert while the profile looked correct. Verified with raw `sandbox-exec`: the `/tmp/…` form exits 1 (`Operation not permitted`), the `/private/tmp/…` form exits 0.

The wrapped command now passes the profile inline (`sandbox-exec -p '<profile>' bash -c …`) instead of staging it in a file under the temp dir. The temp dir is inside the write grant (see below), so a staged profile there could be rewritten by a still-running sandboxed process before a later call's `sandbox-exec` read it; with no file there is nothing to race, and no per-call profile files accumulate in the temp dir any more.

## Behaviour changes you may notice (macOS, `guardrails.sandbox_macos_enabled: true`)

- **The temp-dir write grant is now effective.** Every wrapped command has always been given write access to `os.tmpdir()`. On macOS that is the per-user `$TMPDIR` (`/var/folders/<xx>/<yyyy>/T`), which sits under the `/var` link, so the grant never matched and temp writes were denied. It now matches: wrapped commands can write anywhere under `$TMPDIR`, including files other processes of the same user keep there. The grant is a whole-temp-tree allowance, not one scratch directory per command, and it is wider than the per-run temp of the Linux executor (`--tmpfs`) and of the Windows native runner (a per-run `temp_root`); the Wind

# Fragment-gate hardening: fail-closed quality gate, NUL-safe cleanup transport, bounded check-title, dispatch guards

## What

Collated delivery for the fragment-gate follow-up family from the #3276/#3297
review lineage:

- **#3283** — the pending-fragment quality gate no longer passes when git
  cannot answer. Merge-base resolution failures, changed/added diff failures,
  spawned-git timeouts, unusable repository roots (empty or malformed `.git`
  markers), and base-branch probe failures now fail the required `quality`
  context with an infrastructure-labeled message instead of "gate
  inconclusive, passing" — and an added-diff failure is no longer reported as
  an author-facing fragment VIOLATION. The documented non-repository /
  no-base local pass is preserved through positive marker-absence and
  positive ref-absence checks (locale-independent: git stderr is never
  consulted). With a git discovery override set (GIT_DIR et al.) the gate fails closed on a cwd git cannot describe, where the previous gate passed — fail-closed by design. Known limit: a MALFORMED (as opposed to absent) loose base ref
  also yields the ref-absence exit code and takes that documented pass —
  pre-existing behavior identical to the previous gate. `FRAGMENT_CHECK_ENFORCE=0`
  still soft-warns, now explicitly including infrastructure failures, for local runs.
- **#3299** — the `cleanup-release-fragments` arm in
  `release-and-publish.yml` now derives its changed-path list NUL-end-to-end
  (`git status --porcelain=v1 -z` through a jq reducer into the classifier's
  `--paths-format jsonl --changed-file` framing) instead of the legacy
  newline-delimited pipe that C-quoted and split adversarial paths before the
  classifier could see them. The snapshot stays before the cleanup commit,
  and the temp file is trap-cleaned.
- **#3300** — the `check-title` job in `pr-standards.yml` declares
  `timeout-minutes: 10`, closing the last unbounded job in that workflow.
- **#3307** — both dispatched run blocks that interpolate the
  `pr_number` input into `gh api` paths now refuse non-decimal values before
  any call; a concurrency group cancels superseded `pull_request` runs only
  (merge-group and dispatch runs get run-unique groups and are never
  cancelled, keeping merge-queue checks safe); the non-integer
  `changed_files` guard from #3297 and the least-privilege top-level
  permissions posture are pinned by tests that previously did not exist.

## Why

A required check that maps "cannot determine" to "pass" silently approves
user-visible PRs without release notes whenever git hiccups in CI, and a
lossy list transport can flip a required fragment verdict on paths the
classifier never faithfully saw. Both are fail-open shapes in the gate that
owns the repo's release-notes mandate.

## Verification

`tests/unit/scripts/check-pending-fragment-git.test.ts` (10 tests: real-git
failure legs plus `_internals.spawnSync` seam legs for deterministic timeout
and per-call failure shapes), `fragment-gate-cleanup-transport-3299.test.ts`
(byte-faithful reducer over synthetic porcelain `-z` records including quote-,
newline-, rename- and copy-bearing paths, plus full-pipeline composition on a
real scratch repository), `pr-standards-dispatch-guard-3307.test.ts`
(executed extracted run blocks with a call-recording `gh` stub, both
surfaces), `workflow-hardening.test.ts` (check-title bound, verbatim
concurrency expressions, permissions pin), and
`fragment-gate-workflow-contract.test.ts` (non-integer `changed_files` pin;
cleanup-arm mapping tests kept green).
<!-- custom-release-notes:end -->
